# Learning theories: Piaget, Vygotsky, Bruner, Skinner

## Why this topic matters for the Vice Principal test

**These four names are the core of B.Ed. learning theory, and objective questions test them by swapping their ideas across each other.** The 2026 CRT syllabus (Advt 51/2026) lists "Pedagogy in Education" as one of its eight topics. The closest earlier paper is the 2022 Vice Principal recruitment test (Advt 10/2022). Its file name suggests a General Ability plus Education format, and the education part of such papers leans on B.Ed. psychology: stages, key terms, famous quotations and classroom applications. The questions are rarely deep. The traps are almost always attribution (who said what), sequence (which stage comes first) and sign (reinforcement versus punishment).

Read this pack in order. The three schools come first, then each theorist, then a comparison, then the traps.

## The three schools at a glance

**Behaviourism studies observable behaviour, cognitivism studies mental processes, constructivism studies how learners build knowledge.**

| School | Core claim | Key names |
|---|---|---|
| Behaviourism | Learning = change in observable behaviour through stimulus, response and consequence | Pavlov, Thorndike, Watson, **Skinner** |
| Cognitivism | Learning = change in mental structures; insight, memory, information processing | Köhler, Tolman, **Bruner**, Ausubel, Gagné |
| Constructivism | Learner actively constructs knowledge from experience | **Piaget** (cognitive), **Vygotsky** (social) |

Bruner sits on the border of cognitivism and constructivism. Exam setters usually label him a **cognitive psychologist** and a founder of **discovery learning**.

## Jean Piaget (1896–1980): cognitive constructivism

**Piaget, a Swiss biologist turned psychologist, argued that children build knowledge in a fixed sequence of four stages and that development comes before learning.** He called his field **genetic epistemology** (the study of how knowledge grows). He used the **clinical method**, observing and questioning children, including his own three. He headed the International Bureau of Education in Geneva for decades, which is why his ideas reached school systems so quickly.

### Core concepts

| Term | Meaning | Classroom example |
|---|---|---|
| **Schema** | Mental structure or pattern for organising knowledge | A child's "dog" schema: four legs, fur, barks |
| **Assimilation** | Fitting new information into an existing schema | Calls a cat "dog" |
| **Accommodation** | Changing a schema to fit new information | Learns a new category "cat" |
| **Equilibration** | Balancing assimilation and accommodation; **disequilibrium** drives learning | Confusion about a floating stone pushes the child to revise ideas |

**Adaptation** is the umbrella term for assimilation plus accommodation. **Organisation** is the tendency to link schemas into systems.

### The four stages

The **sequence is invariant and universal**, but ages are approximate. A child cannot skip a stage.

| Stage and age | Hallmarks | Limits |
|---|---|---|
| **Sensorimotor** (0–2) | Learns through senses and movement; **object permanence** emerges around 8 months; deferred imitation and first symbols near age 2 | No mental representation at first |
| **Preoperational** (2–7) | **Symbolic function**: language, pretend play; intuitive thought | **Egocentrism**, **animism**, **centration**, **irreversibility**, no conservation |
| **Concrete operational** (7–11) | **Conservation**, **reversibility**, **decentration**, **seriation**, **classification**, **transitivity** | Logic only on concrete objects, not on hypotheses |
| **Formal operational** (11 onward) | **Abstract**, **hypothetico-deductive**, propositional reasoning; systematic testing of variables | Adolescent egocentrism (imaginary audience, personal fable, described by Elkind) |

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Sensorimotor (0–2): object permanence"] --> B["Preoperational (2–7): egocentrism"]
    B --> C["Concrete operational (7–11): conservation"]
    C --> D["Formal operational (11+): abstract reasoning"]
```

Vocabulary UPSC expects you to decode:

- **Object permanence**: knowing an object exists when out of sight (peek-a-boo works because the baby lacks it).
- **Egocentrism**: inability to take another person's viewpoint; tested with the **three mountains task** (Piaget and Inhelder).
- **Animism**: giving life and feelings to objects ("the sun is tired").
- **Centration**: focusing on one feature only, such as the height of a glass and not its width.
- **Conservation**: understanding that quantity stays the same when shape or arrangement changes. Number is conserved first (about age 6–7), then mass and liquid, weight (about 9) and volume (about 11–12). This staggered mastery within one stage is called **horizontal décalage**.
- **Reversibility**: mentally undoing an action (if 3 + 4 = 7, then 7 − 4 = 3).
- **Seriation**: ordering by size or another dimension. **Transitivity**: if A > B and B > C then A > C.
- **Hypothetico-deductive reasoning**: forming hypotheses and testing them systematically, as in the **pendulum task**.

### Piaget on moral development

Piaget's *The Moral Judgment of the Child* (**1932**) describes a shift from **heteronomous morality** (moral realism: rules are fixed, judged by consequences, belief in immanent justice) to **autonomous morality** (moral relativism: rules are agreements, intentions matter). **Kohlberg** later built his six stages on this base.

### Educational implications and criticisms

Implications: match teaching to the child's stage (**readiness**); use **concrete materials** before abstractions; favour **active discovery**; use **peer interaction** to create disequilibrium; accept that errors reveal thinking. The teacher is a facilitator, not a transmitter.

Criticisms: he **underestimated** young children (later work shows object permanence and some perspective taking appear earlier); stages are less discrete than claimed; many adults never show consistent formal operations; he ignored **culture and instruction**; his samples were small. These criticisms are exactly what Vygotsky's theory answers.

## Lev Vygotsky (1896–1934): sociocultural theory

**Vygotsky, a Russian (Soviet) psychologist who died of tuberculosis at 37, held that learning is social first and individual second, so good teaching can pull development forward.** His major work *Thought and Language* appeared in **1934**, the year he died, and reached the West in English only in **1962**. *Mind in Society* (1978) collected his essays. Because his work was suppressed in the Soviet Union for years, his influence peaked long after his death.

### Core concepts

- **Social constructivism / sociocultural theory**: knowledge is constructed through interaction with others within a culture.
- **General genetic law of cultural development**: every higher function appears **twice**, first between people (**interpsychological**) and then inside the child (**intrapsychological**). This movement inward is **internalisation**.
- **Cultural tools and psychological tools**: language, number systems, writing, maps and signs **mediate** thinking. Language is the most important tool.
- **Elementary versus higher mental functions**: elementary functions are biological (basic perception, involuntary attention); higher functions (voluntary attention, logical memory, concept formation) are culturally built through tools.
- **Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD)**: the gap between what a learner can do **alone** and what the learner can do **with guidance** from a **More Knowledgeable Other (MKO)**, who may be an adult or a more capable peer. Teaching should aim inside the ZPD, not at what the child already does or at what is far beyond reach.
- **Scaffolding**: temporary support that is gradually withdrawn as competence grows. Note the attribution trap: the word was introduced by **Wood, Bruner and Ross (1976)**, not by Vygotsky, though it describes his idea.
- **Learning leads development**: the opposite of Piaget. "What a child can do with assistance today she will be able to do by herself tomorrow."
- **Private speech**: children talking to themselves while working. Vygotsky saw it as a **tool of thought and self-regulation** that later becomes **inner speech**. Piaget called the same behaviour **egocentric speech** and treated it as immaturity that fades. The Vygotskian sequence is **social speech → private (egocentric) speech → inner speech**.

### Classroom applications

**Cooperative learning**, **peer tutoring**, **reciprocal teaching**, **guided participation**, **dynamic assessment** (assessing what the child can do with help, not only alone), and **differentiated instruction** that targets each learner's ZPD. The teacher is a mediator and co-constructor. Multilingual, culturally rooted teaching, including use of the home language in the early grades, fits Vygotsky's view of language as the main tool of thought.

## Piaget versus Vygotsky

**Both are constructivists; Piaget is individual and biological, Vygotsky is social and cultural.**

| Dimension | Piaget | Vygotsky |
|---|---|---|
| Source of knowledge | Child's own action on objects | Social interaction, culture |
| Learning and development | **Development precedes learning** | **Learning leads development** |
| Stages | Four universal stages | No fixed stages; ZPD varies |
| Language | Product of thought | **Tool that shapes thought** |
| Child's self-talk | Egocentric, fades | Private speech, becomes inner speech |
| Role of teacher | Facilitator; provide materials and readiness | Mediator; scaffold within ZPD |
| Peers | Create cognitive conflict | More capable peers teach |

## Jerome Bruner (1915–2016): discovery, structure and the spiral

**Bruner, an American cognitive psychologist, is the name behind discovery learning, the spiral curriculum and the three modes of representation, and he co-coined the term scaffolding.** He co-founded the **Harvard Center for Cognitive Studies (1960)** with George Miller and helped start the "cognitive revolution" against behaviourism. He also wrote the introduction to the 1962 English edition of Vygotsky's *Thought and Language*, carrying Vygotsky's ideas into Western classrooms.

### Key works and ideas

| Work | Year | Idea |
|---|---|---|
| *A Study of Thinking* (with Goodnow and Austin) | **1956** | Concept formation and concept attainment strategies; basis of the Concept Attainment Model |
| *The Process of Education* | **1960** | Report of the 1959 **Woods Hole** conference; structure of the discipline; readiness; intuitive and analytic thinking; motives for learning |
| *Toward a Theory of Instruction* | **1966** | Three modes of representation; four features of a theory of instruction |
| *Actual Minds, Possible Worlds* | 1986 | **Narrative** versus **paradigmatic** (logico-scientific) modes of thought |
| *The Culture of Education* | 1996 | Education as cultural meaning making; "folk pedagogy" |

**Three modes of representation**: **enactive** (knowing through action, as in tying a knot), **iconic** (through images and diagrams), **symbolic** (through language, numbers and symbols). Unlike Piaget's stages, these modes **coexist** in adults and the teacher should move through them in that order when introducing a new concept.

**Spiral curriculum**: key ideas are revisited at increasing depth across grades, so the structure of a discipline is grasped early and refined later. His famous claim from *The Process of Education*: **"Any subject can be taught effectively in some intellectually honest form to any child at any stage of development."**

**Discovery learning**: learners find principles themselves through guided inquiry rather than reception. Bruner expected it to raise intrinsic motivation, memory and problem-solving transfer. Ausubel's **meaningful reception learning** with **advance organisers** is the standard counter position.

**Four features of a theory of instruction** (1966): the learner's **predisposition** to learn, the **structure** of knowledge so that it can be grasped, the most effective **sequence** of presentation, and the nature and pacing of **rewards and punishments** (reinforcement).

Bruner's **MACOS** project (*Man: A Course of Study*) applied these ideas to a social studies curriculum. In later life he moved closer to Vygotsky and stressed culture, narrative and meaning.

## B. F. Skinner (1904–1990): operant conditioning

**Skinner, an American radical behaviourist, explained learning through consequences: behaviour followed by reinforcement is strengthened, behaviour followed by punishment or no consequence weakens.** He built the **Skinner box** (operant chamber) for rats and pigeons and the first widely known **teaching machine**. Key works: *The Behavior of Organisms* (**1938**), *Walden Two* (1948), *Science and Human Behavior* (**1953**), the article "The Science of Learning and the Art of Teaching" (**1954**), *Verbal Behavior* (**1957**, attacked by Chomsky in 1959), *The Technology of Teaching* (**1968**) and *Beyond Freedom and Dignity* (1971).

### Respondent versus operant

Pavlov's classical conditioning is **respondent** or **Type S** conditioning: a stimulus elicits an involuntary response. Skinner's operant conditioning is **Type R** or **instrumental**: the organism emits a voluntary response and the **consequence** determines whether it recurs. Thorndike's **Law of Effect** was the precursor.

### Reinforcement and punishment: the 2 × 2 that UPSC loves

| | Stimulus **added** | Stimulus **removed** |
|---|---|---|
| **Behaviour increases** | **Positive reinforcement** (praise, stars, marks) | **Negative reinforcement** (homework completed, so no detention; seat belt stops the buzzer) |
| **Behaviour decreases** | **Positive punishment** (scolding, extra work) | **Negative punishment** (time-out, loss of play period, **response cost**) |

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Consequence follows behaviour"] --> B["Stimulus added (positive)"]
    A --> C["Stimulus removed (negative)"]
    B --> D["Behaviour increases: positive reinforcement"]
    B --> E["Behaviour decreases: positive punishment"]
    C --> F["Behaviour increases: negative reinforcement"]
    C --> G["Behaviour decreases: negative punishment"]
```

Rules to remember: **positive** means something is added, **negative** means something is taken away. **Reinforcement always increases** behaviour, **punishment always decreases** it. Negative reinforcement is **not** punishment. Skinner himself argued that punishment is weak and temporary and preferred **extinction** plus positive reinforcement of alternatives.

Other terms: **primary reinforcers** (food, water) versus **secondary or conditioned reinforcers** (marks, money, tokens); **shaping** by rewarding **successive approximations** of the target behaviour; **chaining** linking behaviours in sequence; **extinction** when reinforcement stops; **spontaneous recovery**; **stimulus generalisation** and **discrimination**. **Token economy** and **behaviour modification** are classroom applications. The **Premack principle** (do the less preferred activity to earn the preferred one, "grandma's rule") is from David Premack, not Skinner.

### Schedules of reinforcement

| Schedule | Reinforce after... | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| **Continuous** | Every correct response | Fast learning, fast extinction |
| **Fixed ratio (FR)** | Set number of responses (every 5th problem) | High rate, pause after reward |
| **Variable ratio (VR)** | Unpredictable number (gambling) | **Highest, steadiest rate; most resistant to extinction** |
| **Fixed interval (FI)** | Set time (weekly test) | **Scallop**: slow then rushed before deadline |
| **Variable interval (VI)** | Unpredictable time (surprise quiz) | Moderate, steady rate |

The **partial reinforcement effect**: behaviour learnt under intermittent schedules resists extinction more than behaviour learnt under continuous reinforcement. Ratio schedules give higher response rates than interval schedules.

### Programmed instruction and teaching machines

Skinner's **linear programmed instruction** rests on **small steps**, **active responding**, **immediate feedback (confirmation)**, **self-pacing** and a **low error rate**. **Norman Crowder** devised **branching (intrinsic) programming** with multiple-choice frames and remedial loops. **Sidney Pressey** had built a mechanical testing machine in the 1920s, but Skinner's 1954 paper made teaching machines famous. **Mastery learning** and Keller's Personalised System of Instruction are descendants. So are drill-and-practice apps and adaptive learning software today.

### Classroom applications and limits

Behaviourist techniques: clear behavioural objectives (Mager), **contingency contracts**, token economies, time-out, response cost, praise schedules, immediate feedback, drill for fluency. Limits: ignores meaning, motivation and understanding; extrinsic rewards can undermine intrinsic motivation; Chomsky showed that language cannot be explained by reinforcement alone.

## Other names that appear beside these four

**UPSC often adds a fifth option from this list, so learn the one-line tag for each.**

| Theorist | Tag |
|---|---|
| Pavlov | Classical conditioning; dog, bell, salivation; UCS, CS, CR |
| Thorndike | Trial and error; connectionism; laws of **readiness, exercise, effect**; cat in puzzle box |
| Watson | Founder of behaviourism; **Little Albert** |
| Köhler | **Insight learning**; chimpanzee Sultan; Gestalt |
| Tolman | **Latent learning**, **cognitive maps**; sign learning |
| Bandura | **Social learning / observational learning**; **Bobo doll**; attention, retention, reproduction, motivation; self-efficacy |
| Ausubel | **Meaningful reception learning**; **advance organisers** |
| Gagné | **Eight types of learning** hierarchy; **nine events of instruction** |
| Kohlberg | Six stages of moral reasoning in three levels |
| Erikson | Eight psychosocial stages |

## Link to NEP 2020, NCF and the Delhi classroom

**The 5+3+3+4 design of NEP 2020 is a stage theory in policy form.** NEP 2020 (para 4.1) says the curricular and pedagogical structure must correspond to the developmental needs of learners at ages **3–8, 8–11, 11–14 and 14–18**. The Foundational stage is **play and activity based** (Piaget's preoperational child, Bruner's enactive mode). The Preparatory stage adds **discovery and interactive classroom learning** (concrete operations, iconic mode). The Middle stage introduces **experiential learning within subjects** and the Secondary stage **critical thinking and multidisciplinary study** (formal operations, symbolic mode). The mapping to Piaget and Bruner is an interpretation, not wording from NEP.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Foundational (3–8): play based"] --> B["Preparatory (8–11): discovery learning"]
    B --> C["Middle (11–14): experiential learning"]
    C --> D["Secondary (14–18): critical thinking"]
```

**NCF 2005** made **constructivism** the official pedagogy of Indian schools and criticised rote learning; the **NCF for the Foundational Stage (2022)** and the **NCF for School Education (2023)** keep this, with explicit use of play, toys, stories and the home language, which fits Vygotsky's social and language-based view of learning. **NIPUN Bharat (2021)**, the mission for foundational literacy and numeracy, likewise stresses play-based and activity-based learning. In Delhi government schools the earlier activity-based programmes, the **Happiness Curriculum** and **Mission Buniyaad** (both 2018), were replaced in **September 2025** by new programmes, including **Science of Living**, **NEEEV** and **Rashtraneeti**. A Vice Principal supervises this kind of experiential teaching. Competency-based assessment under **PARAKH** asks for application, not recall, which is a Bruner and Piaget position rather than a Skinner one.

## Common traps

- **Scaffolding is not Vygotsky's word.** Wood, Bruner and Ross coined it in 1976. ZPD is Vygotsky's; scaffolding is the teaching strategy built on ZPD.
- **Negative reinforcement is not punishment.** Negative reinforcement removes something unpleasant and increases behaviour. Time-out and response cost are negative punishment.
- **Development precedes learning (Piaget) versus learning leads development (Vygotsky).** Option writers reverse them.
- **Bruner's modes are not stages.** Enactive, iconic and symbolic coexist; Piaget's four stages are sequential and age linked.
- **Spiral curriculum is Bruner**, not Piaget, even though it uses readiness.
- **Conservation belongs to concrete operations**, not to the preoperational stage; the preoperational child fails conservation.
- **Object permanence is sensorimotor**, not preoperational.
- **Hypothetico-deductive reasoning is formal operational**; transitivity and seriation are concrete operational.
- **Egocentric speech**: immaturity for Piaget, tool of thought for Vygotsky.
- **Type S is Pavlov, Type R is Skinner.** Thorndike's Law of Effect is the ancestor of operant conditioning. The word "reinforcement" itself already appears in Pavlov's classical conditioning; Skinner made it the centre of operant theory.
- **Variable ratio** gives the highest rate and most resistance to extinction; **fixed interval** gives the scallop.
- **Premack principle** is Premack, **Little Albert** is Watson, **Bobo doll** is Bandura, **insight** is Köhler. None of these is Skinner.
- **Branching programmed instruction is Crowder**, linear is Skinner.
- **The quotation "any subject can be taught... to any child at any stage"** is Bruner (1960), often misattributed to Piaget or Dewey.
- **Piaget's moral stages (heteronomous, autonomous)** are two; Kohlberg's are six.

## Remember for the exam

1. Piaget: Swiss, 1896–1980, genetic epistemology, four stages, development before learning.
2. Stage ages: sensorimotor 0–2, preoperational 2–7, concrete operational 7–11, formal operational 11 onward.
3. Assimilation fits new data into old schemas; accommodation changes the schema; equilibration balances the two.
4. Object permanence (about 8 months) is sensorimotor; conservation, reversibility, seriation, transitivity are concrete operational.
5. Egocentrism is tested by the three mountains task; formal operations by the pendulum task.
6. Vygotsky: Russian (Soviet), 1896–1934, *Thought and Language* 1934, sociocultural theory, learning leads development.
7. ZPD = gap between unaided and assisted performance; MKO guides; scaffolding (Wood, Bruner, Ross 1976) is the support.
8. Speech sequence for Vygotsky: social → private (egocentric) → inner.
9. Bruner: American, 1915–2016, *The Process of Education* 1960, spiral curriculum, discovery learning.
10. Bruner's modes: enactive, iconic, symbolic, in that teaching order, and they coexist.
11. Bruner's theory of instruction (1966): predisposition, structure, sequence, reinforcement.
12. Skinner: American, 1904–1990, operant (Type R) conditioning, Skinner box, *The Behavior of Organisms* 1938.
13. Positive = add, negative = remove; reinforcement increases, punishment decreases.
14. Variable ratio: highest and steadiest rate, most resistant to extinction; fixed interval: scallop.
15. Programmed instruction: Skinner linear, Crowder branching; Pressey built an earlier testing machine in the 1920s.
16. NEP 2020 stages 3–8, 8–11, 11–14, 14–18 map onto Piaget's stages and Bruner's modes; NCF 2005 made constructivism official.

mcqs.q_en: The concept of the 'Zone of Proximal Development' (ZPD) was given by:
mcqs.q_hi: 'समीपस्थ विकास का क्षेत्र' (ZPD) की अवधारणा किसने दी?
mcqs.explain_en: ZPD is Vygotsky's term for the gap between what a learner can do alone and with guidance from a more knowledgeable other. Bruner is associated with the related term scaffolding, Piaget with stages and Skinner with operant conditioning.
mcqs.explain_hi: ZPD वाइगोत्स्की का शब्द है: शिक्षार्थी अकेले जो कर सकता है और किसी अधिक जानकार व्यक्ति के मार्गदर्शन से जो कर सकता है, उनके बीच का अंतर। ब्रूनर संबंधित शब्द 'स्कैफोल्डिंग' (पाड़) से, पियाजे अवस्थाओं से और स्किनर क्रियाप्रसूत अनुबंधन से जुड़े हैं।
mcqs.source: Vygotsky, Mind in Society (1978); IGNOU BES-123 Block 1

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements about Piaget's theory of cognitive development:
1. Object permanence develops during the sensorimotor stage.
2. Conservation of quantity is achieved during the preoperational stage.
3. Hypothetico-deductive reasoning is a characteristic of the formal operational stage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
पियाजे के संज्ञानात्मक विकास सिद्धांत के बारे में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. वस्तु स्थायित्व संवेदी-गामक अवस्था में विकसित होता है।
2. मात्रा का संरक्षण पूर्व-संक्रियात्मक अवस्था में प्राप्त होता है।
3. परिकल्पनात्मक-निगमनात्मक तर्क औपचारिक संक्रियात्मक अवस्था की विशेषता है।
ऊपर दिए गए कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: Object permanence emerges in the sensorimotor stage and hypothetico-deductive reasoning marks formal operations. Statement 2 is wrong because conservation is achieved in the concrete operational stage; the preoperational child fails conservation tasks.
mcqs.explain_hi: वस्तु स्थायित्व संवेदी-गामक अवस्था में उभरता है और परिकल्पनात्मक-निगमनात्मक तर्क औपचारिक संक्रियात्मक अवस्था की पहचान है। कथन 2 गलत है, क्योंकि संरक्षण मूर्त संक्रियात्मक अवस्था में प्राप्त होता है; पूर्व-संक्रियात्मक बच्चा संरक्षण कार्यों में असफल रहता है।
mcqs.source: Piaget's stage theory; NCERT Psychology XI Ch 3 (Human Development)

mcqs.q_en:
Match List I (concept) with List II (theorist) and select the correct code.
List I: A. Enactive, iconic and symbolic modes; B. Assimilation and accommodation; C. Variable-ratio schedule of reinforcement; D. Inner speech
List II: 1. Piaget; 2. Skinner; 3. Vygotsky; 4. Bruner
mcqs.q_hi:
सूची I (अवधारणा) को सूची II (सिद्धांतकार) से सुमेलित कीजिए और सही कूट चुनिए।
सूची I: A. क्रियात्मक, प्रतिमात्मक और प्रतीकात्मक विधाएँ; B. आत्मसातीकरण और समायोजन; C. पुनर्बलन की परिवर्ती-अनुपात अनुसूची; D. आंतरिक वाक्
सूची II: 1. पियाजे; 2. स्किनर; 3. वाइगोत्स्की; 4. ब्रूनर
mcqs.explain_en: Modes of representation are Bruner's, assimilation and accommodation are Piaget's, reinforcement schedules are Skinner's and inner speech is Vygotsky's. The other codes swap Piaget with Bruner, Vygotsky with Skinner, or Piaget with Vygotsky.
mcqs.explain_hi: प्रतिनिधित्व की विधाएँ ब्रूनर की, आत्मसातीकरण और समायोजन पियाजे के, पुनर्बलन अनुसूचियाँ स्किनर की और आंतरिक वाक् वाइगोत्स्की की अवधारणा है। अन्य कूट पियाजे और ब्रूनर, वाइगोत्स्की और स्किनर, या पियाजे और वाइगोत्स्की को आपस में बदल देते हैं।
mcqs.source: Bruner, Toward a Theory of Instruction (1966); Piaget; Skinner; Vygotsky, Thought and Language

mcqs.q_en: A teacher announces that any student who submits all homework on time during the week will be exempted from the Friday class test, and homework submission rises. In Skinner's terms this is an example of:
mcqs.q_hi: एक शिक्षक घोषणा करता है कि जो विद्यार्थी सप्ताह भर सारा गृहकार्य समय पर जमा करेगा, उसे शुक्रवार की कक्षा परीक्षा से छूट मिलेगी, और गृहकार्य जमा करने की दर बढ़ जाती है। स्किनर की शब्दावली में यह किसका उदाहरण है?
mcqs.explain_en: An unpleasant stimulus (the test) is removed and the behaviour increases, which is negative reinforcement. Positive reinforcement would add a pleasant stimulus; both forms of punishment decrease behaviour, which is not what happened here.
mcqs.explain_hi: एक अप्रिय उद्दीपक (परीक्षा) हटाया जाता है और व्यवहार बढ़ता है, इसलिए यह ऋणात्मक पुनर्बलन है। धनात्मक पुनर्बलन में कोई सुखद उद्दीपक जोड़ा जाता; दंड के दोनों रूप व्यवहार को घटाते हैं, जो यहाँ नहीं हुआ।
mcqs.source: Skinner, Science and Human Behavior (1953); NCERT Psychology XI Ch 5 (Learning)

mcqs.q_en: Which schedule of reinforcement produces the highest and steadiest rate of response and is most resistant to extinction?
mcqs.q_hi: पुनर्बलन की कौन-सी अनुसूची सबसे ऊँची और सबसे स्थिर अनुक्रिया दर उत्पन्न करती है और विलोप के प्रति सबसे अधिक प्रतिरोधी होती है?
mcqs.explain_en: Variable ratio reinforcement, as in gambling, yields the highest steady response rate and the greatest resistance to extinction. Fixed interval produces the scallop pattern; fixed ratio produces a pause after each reward; variable interval gives a moderate steady rate.
mcqs.explain_hi: परिवर्ती अनुपात पुनर्बलन (जैसे जुए में) सबसे ऊँची स्थिर अनुक्रिया दर और विलोप के प्रति सबसे अधिक प्रतिरोध देता है। नियत अंतराल 'स्कैलप' पैटर्न देता है, नियत अनुपात हर पुरस्कार के बाद ठहराव लाता है और परिवर्ती अंतराल मध्यम स्थिर दर देता है।
mcqs.source: Ferster and Skinner, Schedules of Reinforcement (1957); NCERT Psychology XI Ch 5

mcqs.q_en: 'Any subject can be taught effectively in some intellectually honest form to any child at any stage of development.' This statement was made by:
mcqs.q_hi: 'कोई भी विषय किसी बौद्धिक रूप से ईमानदार रूप में, विकास की किसी भी अवस्था में, किसी भी बच्चे को प्रभावी ढंग से पढ़ाया जा सकता है।' यह कथन किसका है?
mcqs.explain_en: The sentence opens the readiness chapter of Bruner's The Process of Education (1960) and underlies his spiral curriculum. It is often misattributed to Piaget, whose readiness view is actually more restrictive.
mcqs.explain_hi: यह वाक्य ब्रूनर की पुस्तक 'द प्रोसेस ऑफ एजुकेशन' (1960) के तत्परता (readiness) वाले अध्याय की शुरुआत में है और उनकी सर्पिल पाठ्यचर्या का आधार है। इसे अक्सर गलती से पियाजे का मान लिया जाता है, जबकि पियाजे का तत्परता संबंधी दृष्टिकोण अधिक प्रतिबंधात्मक है।

mcqs.q_en:
Assertion (A): Vygotsky regarded a child's private (egocentric) speech as a tool of thinking and self-regulation that later becomes inner speech.
Reason (R): Piaget regarded egocentric speech as a sign of cognitive immaturity that fades as the child develops.
Select the correct answer.
mcqs.q_hi:
अभिकथन (A): वाइगोत्स्की ने बच्चे की निजी (आत्मकेंद्रित) वाक् को चिंतन और आत्म-नियमन का साधन माना, जो आगे चलकर आंतरिक वाक् बन जाती है।
कारण (R): पियाजे ने आत्मकेंद्रित वाक् को संज्ञानात्मक अपरिपक्वता का संकेत माना, जो बच्चे के विकास के साथ लुप्त हो जाती है।
सही उत्तर चुनिए।
options_en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
options_hi: A और R दोनों सही हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या है
A और R दोनों सही हैं, परंतु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है
A सही है, परंतु R गलत है
A गलत है, परंतु R सही है
mcqs.explain_en: Both statements correctly describe the two theorists, but Piaget's view does not explain Vygotsky's position; they are opposing interpretations of the same behaviour. Hence both are true and R is not the explanation of A.
mcqs.explain_hi: दोनों कथन दोनों सिद्धांतकारों का सही वर्णन करते हैं, परंतु पियाजे का मत वाइगोत्स्की के मत की व्याख्या नहीं करता; ये एक ही व्यवहार की परस्पर विरोधी व्याख्याएँ हैं। अतः दोनों सही हैं और R, A की व्याख्या नहीं है।
mcqs.source: Vygotsky, Thought and Language (1934); Piaget, The Language and Thought of the Child (1923)

mcqs.q_en: A curriculum in which key concepts are revisited in successive grades at increasing levels of depth and abstraction is called a spiral curriculum. It is associated with:
mcqs.q_hi: वह पाठ्यचर्या जिसमें प्रमुख अवधारणाओं को उत्तरोत्तर कक्षाओं में बढ़ती गहराई और अमूर्तता के साथ दोहराया जाता है, सर्पिल पाठ्यचर्या कहलाती है। यह किससे संबद्ध है?
mcqs.explain_en: The spiral curriculum is Bruner's proposal in The Process of Education (1960) for teaching the structure of a discipline early and refining it later. Piaget's readiness idea is related but the spiral curriculum is not his; Skinner's contribution is programmed instruction.
mcqs.explain_hi: सर्पिल पाठ्यचर्या ब्रूनर का प्रस्ताव है ('द प्रोसेस ऑफ एजुकेशन', 1960): किसी विषय की संरचना जल्दी सिखाई जाए और बाद में उसे परिष्कृत किया जाए। पियाजे का तत्परता विचार इससे जुड़ा है, पर सर्पिल पाठ्यचर्या उनकी नहीं है; स्किनर का योगदान अभिक्रमित अनुदेशन है।
mcqs.source: Bruner, The Process of Education (1960); IGNOU BES-123 Block 1

mcqs.q_en: The term 'scaffolding', now used for temporary teacher support within the Zone of Proximal Development, was first introduced by:
mcqs.q_hi: 'स्कैफोल्डिंग' (पाड़) शब्द, जो अब समीपस्थ विकास के क्षेत्र में शिक्षक द्वारा दी जाने वाली अस्थायी सहायता के लिए प्रयुक्त होता है, सबसे पहले किसने प्रस्तुत किया?
options_en: Lev Vygotsky in Thought and Language
Jean Piaget in The Psychology of Intelligence
David Wood, Jerome Bruner and Gail Ross (1976)
B. F. Skinner in The Technology of Teaching
options_hi: लेव वाइगोत्स्की ने 'थॉट एंड लैंग्वेज' में
जीन पियाजे ने 'द साइकोलॉजी ऑफ इंटेलिजेंस' में
डेविड वुड, जेरोम ब्रूनर और गेल रॉस ने (1976)
बी. एफ. स्किनर ने 'द टेक्नोलॉजी ऑफ टीचिंग' में
mcqs.explain_en: Wood, Bruner and Ross coined 'scaffolding' in their 1976 paper on tutoring in problem solving. Vygotsky gave the ZPD concept but never used the word scaffolding, which is the trap in the first option.
mcqs.explain_hi: वुड, ब्रूनर और रॉस ने 1976 में समस्या-समाधान में ट्यूटरिंग पर अपने शोधपत्र में 'स्कैफोल्डिंग' शब्द गढ़ा। वाइगोत्स्की ने ZPD की अवधारणा दी, पर 'स्कैफोल्डिंग' शब्द का प्रयोग कभी नहीं किया; पहला विकल्प इसी भ्रम का जाल है।
mcqs.source: Wood, Bruner and Ross, 'The role of tutoring in problem solving', Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry (1976)

mcqs.q_en: A five-year-old says that the moon is following her home and that the clouds are angry today. According to Piaget, this illustrates:
mcqs.q_hi: एक पाँच वर्ष की बच्ची कहती है कि चाँद उसके पीछे-पीछे घर आ रहा है और आज बादल गुस्से में हैं। पियाजे के अनुसार यह किसका उदाहरण है?
mcqs.explain_en: Attributing life, intention and feelings to inanimate objects is animism, a feature of preoperational thought. Conservation, reversibility and transitivity are achievements of the concrete operational stage, not features of a five-year-old's thinking.
mcqs.explain_hi: निर्जीव वस्तुओं में जीवन, इरादा और भावनाएँ आरोपित करना जीववाद है, जो पूर्व-संक्रियात्मक चिंतन की विशेषता है। संरक्षण, उत्क्रमणीयता और संक्रामकता मूर्त संक्रियात्मक अवस्था की उपलब्धियाँ हैं, पाँच वर्ष के बच्चे के चिंतन की विशेषताएँ नहीं।
mcqs.source: Piaget's preoperational stage; NIOS D.El.Ed 506 Block 1

mcqs.q_en: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic of Piaget's concrete operational stage?
mcqs.q_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी पियाजे की मूर्त संक्रियात्मक अवस्था की विशेषता नहीं है?
mcqs.explain_en: Hypothetico-deductive reasoning, the systematic testing of hypotheses, appears only in the formal operational stage from about age 11. Reversibility, seriation and conservation are all gained during concrete operations (7–11).
mcqs.explain_hi: परिकल्पनात्मक-निगमनात्मक तर्क (परिकल्पनाओं का व्यवस्थित परीक्षण) लगभग 11 वर्ष से औपचारिक संक्रियात्मक अवस्था में ही प्रकट होता है। उत्क्रमणीयता, क्रमबद्धता और संरक्षण, तीनों मूर्त संक्रियात्मक अवस्था (7–11) में प्राप्त होते हैं।
mcqs.source: Piaget's stage theory; NCERT Psychology XI Ch 3

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements about B. F. Skinner's work:
1. Operant conditioning is also described as Type R or instrumental conditioning.
2. Punishment and negative reinforcement both decrease the frequency of a behaviour.
3. Linear programmed instruction uses small steps, active responding and immediate feedback.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
बी. एफ. स्किनर के कार्य के बारे में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. क्रियाप्रसूत अनुबंधन को टाइप R या साधनात्मक अनुबंधन भी कहा जाता है।
2. दंड और ऋणात्मक पुनर्बलन दोनों किसी व्यवहार की आवृत्ति को घटाते हैं।
3. रेखीय अभिक्रमित अनुदेशन में छोटे चरण, सक्रिय अनुक्रिया और तत्काल प्रतिपुष्टि का प्रयोग होता है।
ऊपर दिए गए कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: Skinner's operant conditioning is Type R, as against Pavlov's Type S, and his linear programming rests on small steps, active responding and immediate confirmation. Statement 2 is wrong: negative reinforcement increases behaviour; only punishment decreases it.
mcqs.explain_hi: स्किनर का क्रियाप्रसूत अनुबंधन टाइप R है (पावलॉव का टाइप S के विपरीत), और उनका रेखीय अभिक्रमण छोटे चरणों, सक्रिय अनुक्रिया और तत्काल पुष्टि पर आधारित है। कथन 2 गलत है: ऋणात्मक पुनर्बलन व्यवहार को बढ़ाता है; केवल दंड उसे घटाता है।
mcqs.source: Skinner, The Behavior of Organisms (1938); 'The Science of Learning and the Art of Teaching' (1954)

mcqs.q_en: Which one of the following correctly contrasts Piaget and Vygotsky on the relationship between learning and development?
mcqs.q_hi: अधिगम और विकास के संबंध पर पियाजे और वाइगोत्स्की के मतों का सही अंतर निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा है?
options_en: Piaget: development precedes learning; Vygotsky: learning leads development
Piaget: learning leads development; Vygotsky: development precedes learning
Both held that instruction cannot influence the pace of development
Both held that development is driven mainly by cultural tools and language
options_hi: पियाजे: विकास अधिगम से पहले आता है; वाइगोत्स्की: अधिगम विकास को आगे ले जाता है
पियाजे: अधिगम विकास को आगे ले जाता है; वाइगोत्स्की: विकास अधिगम से पहले आता है
दोनों का मत था कि अनुदेशन विकास की गति को प्रभावित नहीं कर सकता
दोनों का मत था कि विकास मुख्यतः सांस्कृतिक उपकरणों और भाषा से संचालित होता है
mcqs.explain_en: Piaget held that a child must reach a developmental stage before certain learning is possible, whereas Vygotsky held that guided learning within the ZPD pulls development forward. The second option reverses the two, and the last two options misstate both theorists.
mcqs.explain_hi: पियाजे के अनुसार कुछ अधिगम तभी संभव है जब बच्चा उपयुक्त विकासात्मक अवस्था तक पहुँच जाए, जबकि वाइगोत्स्की के अनुसार ZPD के भीतर निर्देशित अधिगम विकास को आगे खींचता है। दूसरा विकल्प दोनों को उलट देता है और अंतिम दो विकल्प दोनों सिद्धांतकारों के मत को गलत बताते हैं।
mcqs.source: Vygotsky, Mind in Society (1978); Piaget; IGNOU BES-123 Block 1

mcqs.q_en: In operant conditioning, the technique of reinforcing successive approximations of a desired behaviour until the target behaviour is reached is called:
mcqs.q_hi: क्रियाप्रसूत अनुबंधन में, वांछित व्यवहार तक पहुँचने तक उसके क्रमिक सन्निकटनों को पुनर्बलित करने की तकनीक क्या कहलाती है?
mcqs.explain_en: Shaping rewards closer and closer approximations of the goal behaviour. Chaining links already learnt behaviours in sequence, extinction is the fading of a response when reinforcement stops, and generalisation is responding to similar stimuli.
mcqs.explain_hi: शेपिंग में लक्ष्य व्यवहार के उत्तरोत्तर निकट सन्निकटनों को पुरस्कृत किया जाता है। शृंखलन पहले से सीखे व्यवहारों को क्रम में जोड़ता है, विलोप पुनर्बलन रुकने पर अनुक्रिया का क्षीण होना है, और सामान्यीकरण मिलते-जुलते उद्दीपकों पर अनुक्रिया करना है।
mcqs.source: Skinner, Science and Human Behavior (1953); NCERT Psychology XI Ch 5

mcqs.q_en: A Class 6 mathematics teacher introduces fractions by first having students fold and cut paper strips, then showing shaded diagrams, and finally writing 1/2 + 1/4 on the board. This sequence follows Bruner's modes of representation in the order:
mcqs.q_hi: कक्षा 6 का गणित शिक्षक भिन्नों का परिचय पहले विद्यार्थियों से कागज़ की पट्टियाँ मोड़कर और काटकर, फिर छायांकित आरेख दिखाकर और अंत में बोर्ड पर 1/2 + 1/4 लिखकर कराता है। यह क्रम ब्रूनर की प्रतिनिधित्व विधाओं के किस क्रम का अनुसरण करता है?
mcqs.explain_en: Folding paper is enactive (action), diagrams are iconic (images) and written notation is symbolic, which is Bruner's recommended teaching order. The last option lists Piaget's stages, which are developmental stages and not modes of representation.
mcqs.explain_hi: कागज़ मोड़ना क्रियात्मक (क्रिया), आरेख प्रतिमात्मक (चित्र) और लिखित संकेतन प्रतीकात्मक विधा है; यही ब्रूनर का अनुशंसित शिक्षण क्रम है। अंतिम विकल्प पियाजे की अवस्थाएँ बताता है, जो विकासात्मक अवस्थाएँ हैं, प्रतिनिधित्व की विधाएँ नहीं।
mcqs.source: Bruner, Toward a Theory of Instruction (1966)

Hindi: added q_hi, options_hi and explain_hi for all 15 MCQs (the pack had none), with option order identical to English.
Q3 explanation: the wrong codes also swap Piaget with Vygotsky (option C: B-3, D-1); explanation now names all three swaps.
